_about: What kind of place the character grew up in. 'urban' entries may reuse the character's current base city. Original content written for DCUGen.

kinds.text: a rust-belt mill town where the smokestacks went cold one by one
a sprawling suburb of identical houses and cul-de-sacs
a dense inner-city neighborhood where everyone knew everyone's business
a housing project where the elevators worked about half the time
a fishing village where the tides set the clock
a farming county where the nearest movie theater was forty minutes away
a desert town built around a military base
a mountain town where winter lasted half the year
a college town that emptied out every summer
an oil-boom town that boomed, busted and boomed again
a company town owned, practically, by {company}
kinds.hook: {company} still owns half the town and is hiding something under the old plant.

kinds.text: a gentrifying neighborhood where the corner bodega became a juice bar
a tourist beach town that was magical in July and desolate in February
an immigrant enclave where three languages were spoken on every block
a border town with family on both sides of the line
a river port with barges, bars and a long history of smuggling
a wealthy gated enclave with private security on every corner
an old-money neighborhood of brownstones and private schools
a shrinking prairie town with more grain elevators than people
a swampy bayou parish where the roads flooded every spring
a mining town where the mountain had been hollowed out for a century
a high-crime waterfront district the tourist maps leave blank
a planned 'city of tomorrow' that never quite arrived
a sleepy town that made national news when something crashed in a nearby field
kinds.hook: Whatever crashed outside {hometown} was never fully recovered.

kinds.text: a town that was rebuilt after a villain's weather machine flattened it
a neighborhood in the shadow of a hero team's headquarters, where capes overhead were normal
a reservation community with deep roots and few jobs
an island community reachable only by ferry
a downtown loft district of artists and abandoned warehouses
a commuter town where the parents left before dawn and got home after dark
a military housing district that changed faces every year
a ski-resort town full of seasonal workers and absentee owners
a crumbling industrial port being slowly bought up by developers
a megacity district so large it felt like its own country
a quiet town with an unusually high number of unsolved disappearances
kinds.hook: The disappearances in {hometown} have started again.

kinds.text: a religious community that kept apart from the outside world
a trailer park on the edge of an interstate
a tech-boom suburb where every parent worked at a startup
a town next to a sprawling chemical plant that glowed faintly at night
kinds.hook: The chemical plant outside {hometown} is reopening under new management.

kinds.text: a capital city full of embassies, motorcades and protests
